notes.swap: the paper's lens-coordinate swap: V = [v_a v_t] (columns), c = pinv(V) @ h, sigma(c) = flip(c) (the two coordinates exchange), h' = h + swap_alpha * V @ (sigma(c) - c); v_x = (W_U J_l)[x] rows (interventions.lens_vectors convention, keyed by token id instead of string). Applied in-forward by per-layer hooks on model.layers[l] (x16 SinkClamper pattern): the prefill forward swaps every row in the arm's position mask; each single-token decode forward swaps the new token's row for the text/all scopes (image positions do not recur under KV caching)
notes.handoff: the handoff position is the LAST PROMPT token (the prefill forward's decoding position, whose distribution predicts generated token 0; the x14 step_records[0] convention) — here the row residual[-1] of the recorded prefill
notes.target: target t: a COCO category annotated on OTHER images (never on this one), not the answer's own category, whose emission id is not among the model's top-10 next-token ids at the handoff position and whose name does not word-match the decoded top-10; tiers relax the top-10 exclusions in order (string+id -> id-only -> none) and the tier used is recorded; the choice is seeded per image
notes.matcher: x13 detect_mentions matcher: one whole-sequence decode, lowercased, category names matched longest-first with word boundaries, optional (s|es) plural suffix, span masking (so 'hot dog' does not also match 'dog'); irregular plurals are a documented gap
notes.topk: top-k = the k highest calibrated J-lens logits at the position; membership counts a token's emission id (last subword of ' ' + name) among the k ids

interpretation_limits: the prompt NAMES one of the image's annotated categories, so the baseline answer is usually that category (or a variant); the swap tests whether the answer concept can be redirected once it exists, not comprehension
'What {plural-only category} is in the picture?' is ungrammatical for a few COCO names (scissors, skis); the template is kept verbatim by design
flip_string scans the whole answer for the target word (an answer like 'a dog' flips by string even when token 0 is the article); flip_token is the strict first-token readout
only text/all scopes swap decode steps: with KV caching the decode forward carries exactly the new (text) token, and image positions do not recur
a single swap layer is armed at a time; interactions between simultaneous layers are untested (x16 convention)
the tiny backend is a random-weight fixture: it exercises the machinery, its flip rates do not transfer to the real model
